recognize_zh: 中央一顆分葉的嗜中性球，細胞質有細顆粒；標題為 Barr body（鼓槌狀附屬體，drumstick），但在此解析度下無法清楚分辨與核葉相連的小圓形附屬體，需高倍確認，屬部分吻合。
features: Single segmented neutrophil with three to four nuclear lobes and clumped chromatin
A discrete drumstick appendage (about 1.5 microns, attached by a thin chromatin strand) is not clearly resolvable in this image
Background red cells normocytic with central pallor; numerous scattered platelets
Fine stain precipitate across the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single segmented neutrophil with three to four lobes, clumped chromatin and finely granular cytoplasm, set in a background of normocytic red cells, scattered platelets and fine stain precipitate. The title indicates a Barr body (drumstick), a small round chromatin appendage attached to a nuclear lobe by a thin strand, but a definite drumstick cannot be distinguished from overlapping lobes at this resolution. The image is therefore only partially illustrative; drumsticks are a normal finding in female neutrophils (inactivated X chromosome) and have no pathological significance.

ddx.dx: Sessile nodule or small nuclear lobe
ddx.vs: Sessile nodules lack the thin stalk and small nuclei lobes are larger and less dense than a 1.5-micron drumstick.
Hypersegmentation means six or more lobes or more than 5% with five lobes, rather than a single small appendage.
Döhle bodies are pale blue cytoplasmic patches, not dense chromatin attached to the nucleus.
Detached nuclear fragments float free in the cytoplasm without a connecting chromatin strand.
